reason: The sources provide enough verifiable claims to construct a surprising 45-second story with multiple corroborated facts.
story: On October 9, 2022, a cosmic explosion occurred roughly 2.4 billion light-years away in the constellation Sagitta. Dubbed GRB 221009A and nicknamed the BOAT, or Brightest Of All Time, it was caused by a massive star collapsing into a black hole in a Type Ic supernova. The resulting gamma-ray burst was so overwhelmingly intense that it temporarily blinded most space telescopes designed to monitor it. It shattered records by being roughly seventy times brighter than any previous burst ever recorded. Despite originating billions of light-years away, the radiation slammed into Earth's upper atmosphere, ionizing the ionosphere and disturbing longwave radio communications in a manner usually only caused by solar flares from our own nearby Sun.
angle: A cosmic explosion two billion light-years away was so powerful it physically rattled Earth's upper atmosphere and blinded space telescopes.

claims.claim: The gamma-ray burst occurred approximately 2.4 billion light-years away from Earth.
The burst originated in the constellation Sagitta.
It was dubbed the BOAT, standing for Brightest Of All Time.
The event was caused by a massive star undergoing a supernova and giving birth to a black hole.
The burst was so bright it temporarily blinded or saturated most gamma-ray space telescope detectors.
The event was roughly 70 times brighter than the previous record holder.
Lightning detectors in India and Germany picked up signs that Earth's ionosphere was perturbed by the burst.
The burst disrupted longwave radio communications on Earth.
It was jointly discovered by the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope.
The Chinese LHAASO observatory recorded VHE photons including a record 18 TeV of energy from the burst.
It was observed by the James Webb Space Telescope and Hubble Space Telescope.

disputed: Russia's Carpet-2 facility at the Baksan Neutrino Observatory may have recorded a single 251-TeV photon, which is treated tentatively and should be attributed or omitted.
